nodes.summary: The perfect-graph decision problem, which accepts exactly the bitstrings that decode to a valid adjacency-matrix instance whose graph is perfect, lies in the complexity class NP.
nodes.title: Perfect graphs have an NP description

nodes.summary: The perfect-graph decision problem, which accepts exactly the bitstrings that decode to a valid adjacency-matrix instance whose graph is perfect, lies in the complexity class NP: there are a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients and a polynomial-time verifier $R$ on pairs of bitstrings such that a bitstring $x$ is accepted if and only if $R$ accepts $(x, w)$ for some bitstring $w$ of length at most…
nodes.title: Edmonds's question: an NP description of perfect graphs

nodes.summary: A finite simple graph $G$ is perfect if, for every set $S$ of its vertices, the induced subgraph $G[S]$ has chromatic number equal to its clique number, the largest size of a clique in $G[S]$.
nodes.title: Perfect graph

nodes.summary: A finite simple graph $G$ is perfect if and only if its complement $\overline{G}$ is perfect.
nodes.title: Weak perfect graph theorem

nodes.summary: A finite simple graph $G$ is perfect if and only if its complement $\overline{G}$ is perfect.
nodes.title: Lovász's weak perfect graph theorem

nodes.summary: A finite simple graph $G$ satisfies condition (P) if, for every set $S$ of its vertices, the induced subgraph $G[S]$, with independence number $\alpha(G[S])$ and clique number $\omega(G[S])$, satisfies $|S| \le \alpha(G[S]) \cdot \omega(G[S])$.
nodes.title: Gasparian's condition (P)

nodes.summary: An instance consists of a natural number $n$ and a Boolean $n \times n$ matrix $A$ with rows and columns indexed by $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, read as the adjacency matrix of a graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$. The matrix is arbitrary; symmetry and the absence of loops are imposed separately by the validity condition.
nodes.title: Adjacency-matrix graph instance

nodes.summary: The decision problem on bitstrings that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the bitstring encoding of adjacency-matrix instances, to a valid instance whose graph is perfect. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance, or decode to an invalid one, are rejected.
nodes.title: The perfect-graph decision problem

nodes.summary: Every finite perfect graph $G$ satisfies Gasparian's condition (P): for every set $S$ of its vertices, the induced subgraph $G[S]$, with independence number $\alpha(G[S])$ and clique number $\omega(G[S])$, satisfies $|S| \le \alpha(G[S]) \cdot \omega(G[S])$.
nodes.title: Perfect graphs satisfy condition (P)

nodes.summary: A valid instance with $n$ vertices and adjacency matrix $A$ determines the simple graph on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which vertices $x$ and $y$ are adjacent exactly when $A_{xy}$ is true.
nodes.title: Graph of a valid instance

nodes.summary: An instance with $n$ vertices and adjacency matrix $A$ is valid when $A$ is symmetric, that is, $A_{yx}$ is true whenever $A_{xy}$ is true, and has no loops, that is, $A_{xx}$ is false for every vertex $x$.
nodes.title: Valid adjacency-matrix instance
